title: GPU runbook authoring guidelines and canonical template
author: Maya Chen
content:
Purpose:
This page defines standards and a canonical template for writing GPU-related runbooks (capacity, warm pools, network egress, kernel rollouts, preemption events). Aim: reduce ambiguity during incidents, speed up resolution, and make runbooks automatable and testable.

Scope:
- Applies to any runbook that will be used by on-call SREs, infra engineers, and incident commanders for GPU fleet and networking incidents.
- Includes runbooks for: warm-pool depletion, KV-cache inconsistency, cross-account egress failures, preemptive burst fallback, kernel/driver rollouts, and Terraform-driven provisioning failures.

Why a standard matters:
- Faster TTR (time-to-resolution) when playbooks are predictable.
- Easier tooling: alert->runbook linking, validation tests, and automated remediation hooks.
- Consistent postmortem signals (we can measure checklist completion).

Runbook authoring checklist (short):
1) Add metadata header (owner, reviewers, SLOs, labels)
2) Include a 1-line summary and impact matrix
3) Provide quick actions (<5 commands) for restore paths
4) Add structured troubleshooting steps with telemetry queries and thresholds
5) Provide safe rollforward/rollback steps and experiment gating
6) List required permissions and automation hooks (k8s, terraform, cloud CLI)
7) Add post-incident checklist items and test instructions

Required metadata (table):
| field | description | example |
| title | short, descriptive name | GPU warm-pool depletion – rapid recovery |
| owner | single on-call owner (team alias) | infra-gpu-oncall@redwood.com |
| runbook_id | unique id (space/name/date) | eng-infra/gpu/warmpool-depletion-v1 |
| status | draft | in_review | published |
| severity | expected severity if triggered | Sev2 |
| sro_expectation | critical SLOs to consult | warm_pool_availability >= 99.9% |
| last_tested | date of last automated test | 2025-01-14 |

Runbook structure (canonical headings) – authors must include these sections in order:
1) Summary and impact matrix
   - Short 2–3 sentence problem description
   - Who is affected (tenants, dedicated customers, console)
   - Impact levels mapped to metrics (e.g., warm_pool_utilization > 90% -> degraded)
2) Alerts that should link to this runbook
   - Alert rule id, Prometheus/Grafana dashboard link, severity mapping
3) Quick mitigation (safe, fast) – up to five commands
4) Full remediation flow (ordered steps with checks after each step)
5) Rollback behaviour / automatic fallback triggers
6) Owner and escalation (phone/pager/team rotation links)
7) Post-incident validation & follow-up tasks
8) Test instructions and automation hooks

Example: quick mitigation section (format and guidance)
- Purpose: give an operator an immediate, safe hammer to buy time.
- Requirements: runbook must contain at most five quick-restore commands. Each command must include a readable explanation and required privilege level.

Example quick actions for warm-pool depletion:
1) Throttle non-critical eval queues (k8s label change):
   kubectl -n infra set resources deployment/eval-worker --limits=cpu=500m
   (Required: infra-deploy role)
2) Temporarily increase warm-pool target (autoscaler API):
   curl -X POST -H "Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN" https://ops.api.internal/autoscaler/warmpool --data '{"target": 12}'
   (Required: ops-api write)
3) Offload low-priority tenants to burst-account: run tenant-affinity operator command (see step 4 in remediation)

Telemetry and queries (examples to include in runbook)
- Prometheus: 
  - warm_pool_availability (gauge) -- query: warm_pool_available / warm_pool_total < 0.95
  - gpu_preempt_rate (counter) -- query: increase(gpu_preempt_total[5m]) > 50
- Grafana panels to reference: GPU Fleet Overview (dashboard id: infra.gpu.overview)
- Logs: example ELK query: "level:ERROR AND component:allocator AND message:"failed to allocate""

Full remediation flow (recommended structure)
A. Confirm impact and correlate metrics (5 min)
   - Check warm_pool_availability and tenant error rates
   - Confirm SLO breach conditions before escalations
B. Execute quick mitigation actions (document exact commands)
C. Perform targeted remediation steps (drain/recover nodes, rehydrate KV caches)
D. Monitor for stabilization (15–30 min) and run smoke tests (see validation list)
E. If unstable after remediation window, trigger capacity escalation (pg: infra-capacity@redwood.com) and follow the incident bridge template

Rollforward and rollback guidance
- All changes that touch kernel, driver, or TF modules must have a predefined rollback command and artifact version pinned.
- Rollbacks should be tested in the staging warm-pool (runbook must include the test commands and validation queries).
- For Terraform-driven changes: use terraform plan + a canary workspace. Include CLI snippet in runbook: 
  terraform workspace select canary || terraform workspace new canary
  terraform apply -var-file=canary.tfvars
  (Rollback: terraform apply -var-file=canary-rollback.tfvars)

Escalation policy (minimum)
- If metrics still unresponsive after 20 minutes: escalate to SRE lead + oncall infra manager.
- If customer-facing error rate > 5% for > 10m: include product-support and customer-success.
- Pager contacts (example): infra-gpu-oncall PagerDuty: PD-12345; infra-sre-lead Slack: @caleb-morgan

Post-incident checklist (required for published runbooks)
- Mark the timeline in the incident tracker and link to this runbook
- Add root cause hypothesis and data-driven evidence (graphs + logs)
- Schedule a 1-hour postmortem review within 7 days
- Update runbook based on what worked/failed and increment the runbook version
- Add automated test that reproduces the alert condition in the CI harness (CI/CD link)

Template (copy-paste canonical runbook)
---BEGIN RUNBOOK TEMPLATE---
Title: <short descriptive title>
Runbook ID: <space>/<name>/v1
Owner: <team alias or person>
Severity: <Sev2 | Sev3>
SLOs referenced: <warm_pool_availability >= 99.9%>
Last tested: <YYYY-MM-DD>

1) Summary and impact:
   - Summary: <one-liner>
   - Impact: <who & what>

2) Alerts:
   - alert name: <prom-alert-id> | expression: <promql> | severity: <Sev2>

3) Quick mitigation (do these first, in order):
   - cmd1: <command>  // privileges: <role>
   - cmd2: <command>  // privileges: <role>

4) Full remediation (ordered):
   - Step 1: <step details + check commands>
   - Step 2: <step details + check commands>

5) Rollback/rollback-testing:
   - Rollback command(s): <commands>
   - How to test rollback in staging: <instructions>

6) Owner and escalation contacts:
   - primary oncall: <alias> | pager: <pd-id>
   - escalation: <team alias> | slack: <handle>

7) Post-incident tasks:
   - create postmortem, update runbook, add test to CI, schedule follow-up

---END TEMPLATE---

Example runbook excerpt (GPU warm-pool depletion)
- Summary: Warm-pool warm_count fell below soft target; new requests are queued and causing client errors.
- Quick mitigation: throttle eval workloads, bump warmpool target via autoscaler API, promote pre-seeded nodes.
- Remediation detail: check node provisioning events: kubectl get nodes --selector=gpu=true -o wide | grep Pending. If nodes Pending > 0 for > 2m, check cloud provider quota and event log: aws ec2 describe-instances --filters 'Name=tag:role,Values=warmpool'

Automation & CI hooks (must be included in runbook metadata)
- Each published runbook must point to one or more automated tests in our CI harness (path: infra/ci/gpu/runbook-tests). Tests should validate the alert triggers and quick-mitigation idempotency.
- Include the terraform module and GitHub PR template used to change autoscaler defaults (example repo: github.com/redwood-inference/infra-auto-scaler).

Authoring pass & review expectations
- Draft -> peer review by two reviewers (one SRE, one infra engineer) -> runbook automated smoke test -> publish.
- Each reviewer should check: accuracy of commands, privileges are correctly documented, rollback commands are present, telemetry queries show expected signals.

How to publish and version
- File naming: space/subspace/short-name-vX.json (increment vX on substantive changes).
- Before publishing: run the runbook linter (infra/tools/runbook-lint) and run automated smoke test.
- Add last_tested date in header and update labels: runbook-tested, runbook-published.

Appendix: common CLI snippets (don’t rely on these as the single source-of-truth)
- Check warm pool availability (PromQL): 
  (sum(warm_pool_available) by (region) / sum(warm_pool_total) by (region)) < 0.95
- Quick drain command (k8s): kubectl -n infra drain node/<node-name> --ignore-daemonsets --delete-local-data
- Terraform canary apply snippet: 
  cd infra/terraform/autoscaler && terraform workspace select canary || terraform workspace new canary && terraform apply -var-file=ci-canary.tfvars

Questions or suggestions: contact the doc owner (owner field above) or the infra-docs mailing list (infra-docs@redwood.com).
